analyses.title: Highest monthly total order amount
analyses.sql:
WITH payment_per_order AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(amount) AS payment_amount
  FROM payments
  GROUP BY order_id
),
monthly_check AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS order_month,
    SUM(p.payment_amount) AS recomputed_total_order_amount,
    SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_amount IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_amount_orders
  FROM orders AS o
  JOIN payment_per_order AS p
    ON p.order_id = o.order_id
  GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)
)
SELECT
  v.order_month,
  v.total_order_amount,
  c.recomputed_total_order_amount,
  c.null_amount_orders,
  ABS(v.total_order_amount - c.recomputed_total_order_amount) AS amount_difference
FROM monthly_order_summary AS v
JOIN monthly_check AS c
  ON v.order_month = c.order_month
WHERE v.total_order_amount IS NOT NULL
  AND c.null_amount_orders = 0
  AND ABS(v.total_order_amount - c.recomputed_total_order_amount) <= 0.000001
ORDER BY v.total_order_amount DESC
LIMIT 1

notes: Amounts are AUD and include all order statuses; total order amount is not revenue.
Payment amounts were aggregated at order grain before the monthly comparison using the defined orders to payments relationship.
Null amount check passed and the recomputed amount matched within the 0.000001 tolerance.

analyses.title: Total payment amount by payment method
analyses.sql:
WITH payment_totals AS (
  SELECT
    p.payment_method,
    SUM(p.amount) AS total_payment_amount
  FROM payments AS p
  GROUP BY p.payment_method
),
payment_per_order AS (
  SELECT
    p.order_id,
    SUM(p.amount) AS payment_amount
  FROM payments AS p
  GROUP BY p.order_id
),
order_payment_check AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(o.amount) AS total_order_amount,
    SUM(po.payment_amount) AS total_payment_amount,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o.amount IS NULL OR po.payment_amount IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_amount_order_rows
  FROM orders AS o
  LEFT JOIN payment_per_order AS po
    ON po.order_id = o.order_id
),
payment_null_check AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(CASE WHEN p.amount IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_payment_amount_rows,
    SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_method IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_payment_method_rows
  FROM payments AS p
)
SELECT
  pt.payment_method,
  pt.total_payment_amount,
  pnc.null_payment_amount_rows,
  pnc.null_payment_method_rows,
  opc.total_order_amount,
  opc.total_payment_amount AS reconciled_payment_amount,
  opc.total_order_amount - opc.total_payment_amount AS reconciliation_difference,
  opc.null_amount_order_rows,
  ABS(opc.total_order_amount - opc.total_payment_amount) <= 0.000001 AS within_amount_tolerance
FROM payment_totals AS pt
CROSS JOIN payment_null_check AS pnc
CROSS JOIN order_payment_check AS opc
ORDER BY pt.payment_method

Payments were aggregated per order for reconciliation using the defined payments to orders relationship.
Null payment amounts, null payment methods, and null order payment amounts were zero. Reconciliation difference was 0.0, within tolerance 0.000001.

analyses.title: Data-quality checks
analyses.sql:
WITH payment_totals AS (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    SUM(amount) AS payment_amount
  FROM payments
  GROUP BY order_id
),
checks AS (
  SELECT
    'orders_null_key_date_status_amount' AS check_name,
    COUNT(*) AS failure_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE order_id IS NULL
     OR order_date IS NULL
     OR status IS NULL
     OR amount IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'orders_orphan_customers' AS check_name,
    COUNT(*) AS failure_count
  FROM orders
  LEFT JOIN customers
    ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id
  WHERE orders.customer_id IS NOT NULL
    AND customers.customer_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'payments_null_key_or_amount' AS check_name,
    COUNT(*) AS failure_count
  FROM payments
  WHERE payment_id IS NULL
     OR order_id IS NULL
     OR amount IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'payments_orphan_orders' AS check_name,
    COUNT(*) AS failure_count
  FROM payments
  LEFT JOIN orders
    ON payments.order_id = orders.order_id
  WHERE orders.order_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'order_payment_amount_mismatch_over_tolerance' AS check_name,
    COUNT(*) AS failure_count
  FROM orders
  LEFT JOIN payment_totals
    ON orders.order_id = payment_totals.order_id
  WHERE payment_totals.order_id IS NULL
     OR ABS(orders.amount - payment_totals.payment_amount) > 0.000001
)
SELECT
  check_name,
  failure_count,
  CASE WHEN failure_count = 0 THEN 'pass' ELSE 'fail' END AS status
FROM checks
ORDER BY check_name

notes: Wren validated and executed the read-only governed query.
Payment amounts were aggregated at order grain and compared with a tolerance of 0.000001.

analyses.title: Overall average order value
analyses.sql:
WITH payment_totals AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_id,
    SUM(p.amount) AS payment_amount
  FROM orders AS o
  LEFT JOIN payments AS p
    ON p.order_id = o.order_id
  GROUP BY o.order_id
),
checks AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o.amount IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_amount_count,
    SUM(CASE
      WHEN o.amount IS NOT NULL
       AND ABS(o.amount - COALESCE(pt.payment_amount, 0)) > 0.000001
      THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END) AS amount_mismatch_count
  FROM orders AS o
  LEFT JOIN payment_totals AS pt
    ON pt.order_id = o.order_id
),
monthly_check AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(order_count) AS monthly_order_count,
    SUM(total_order_amount) AS monthly_total_order_amount,
    SUM(order_count * average_order_value) AS monthly_reconstructed_total
  FROM monthly_order_summary
)
SELECT
  AVG(o.amount) AS overall_average_order_value_aud,
  c.order_count,
  c.null_amount_count,
  c.amount_mismatch_count,
  m.monthly_order_count,
  m.monthly_total_order_amount,
  m.monthly_reconstructed_total,
  ABS(SUM(o.amount) - m.monthly_total_order_amount) AS monthly_total_tolerance_diff
FROM orders AS o
CROSS JOIN checks AS c
CROSS JOIN monthly_check AS m
GROUP BY
  c.order_count,
  c.null_amount_count,
  c.amount_mismatch_count,
  m.monthly_order_count,
  m.monthly_total_order_amount,
  m.monthly_reconstructed_total

The monthly summary reconciled to the orders total within 0.000001.
